\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 13.2 ``Complete Information'', p.~285 {[}PDF p.~304{]}. Reproduced verbatim. \textbf{Answer in the source:} no (none in the book; Princeton UP's website has about half, not checked).

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Complete Information:} Consider a set of \(N\) players participating in a sealed-bid second-price auction, but assume that there is complete information so that each player knows the valuation of every other player.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Is it still true that each player bidding his valuation is a weakly dominant strategy?
\item
  Are there other Nash equilibria of this game?
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
